documents.text:
Develops optical-system design methods with particular emphasis on freeform surfaces and optics for augmented and virtual reality. His documented work concerns the design of optical systems, rather than general AR software or all forms of gradient-index material fabrication.

Freeform optical-system design
Develops design methods for optical systems using freeform surfaces.

Optics for augmented and virtual reality
Studies optical design for AR and VR applications.

Studies formal and computational semantics, connecting language meaning with syntax, inference and event structure. His research includes propositional-attitude verbs, clause selection and the structure of linguistic events. He also develops computational tools for semantic and video-event annotation, probabilistic programming and sharing research information.

Formal and computational natural-language semantics
Studies language meaning and its relation to syntax, including attitude verbs, clause selection and event structure.

Video-event annotation and semantic tooling
His selected software and presentation describe FOVEA, a tool for video annotation ontologies with automated analysis and object detection.

Probabilistic programming tools
His selected code includes a functional probabilistic programming language for PyTorch.

Studies computational plasma physics for inertial and magneto-inertial fusion and high-energy-density experiments. His stated methods include magnetohydrodynamics and particle-in-cell simulations, with laser-plasma interaction among the applications. An institutional account describes his work on hybrid fluid-kinetic multiphysics simulation and contributions to laser-plasma physics and charged-particle transport.

Inertial and magneto-inertial fusion modeling
Studies inertial and magneto-inertial fusion in a computational plasma-physics program.

Magnetohydrodynamic and particle-in-cell methods
Lists magnetohydrodynamics, computational physics and particle-in-cell simulation among his research methods.

Hybrid fluid-kinetic multiphysics
An attributed institutional report describes development of a hybrid fluid-kinetic simulation code for interpreting HED and fusion experiments.

Designs electrochemical systems through synthetic molecular and materials chemistry, controlling interfaces to improve reaction selectivity and energy efficiency. Her group develops stimuli-responsive electroactive compounds, framework-coated electrodes and methods for tuning nanoscale temperature gradients in catalysis. Applications include sustainable fuels and chemicals, energy conversion/storage and electrochemical sensing.

Electrochemical interface and catalyst microenvironments
Controls chemical and physical properties of electrochemical interfaces to improve selectivity and efficiency.

Stimuli-responsive electroactive materials
Synthesizes compounds whose redox behavior responds to heat and ionic strength for energy conversion and storage.

Porous-framework-coated electrodes
Studies framework-coated electrode structure and catalytic behavior in energy-relevant reactions.

Nanoscale thermal gradients in catalysis
Develops approaches to tune and quantify temperature gradients and use them to influence catalytic reactions.

Studies how surface and interfacial chemistry controls the function of micro- and nanostructured materials. His group develops monomolecular deposition and patterning methods, polymer-based manufacturing approaches and multicomponent colloids with spatially varied chemical, optical and magnetic properties. Experiments combine organic/polymer chemistry, surface characterization and optical or magnetic trapping, connecting precise interface control with scalable fabrication.

Molecular surface chemistry and interface control
Develops monomolecular deposition methods to alter electronic, biological and chemical interface properties without changing bulk composition.

Organic surface functionalization
Studies chemical modification and organic monolayers on inorganic surfaces; the overview emphasizes functional interface control.

Surface patterning and polymer-based manufacturing
Combines deposition and patterning with polymer materials for scalable micro/nanostructured devices.

Anisotropic multicomponent colloids
Develops manufacturing methods for colloids with spatially distributed chemical, optical and magnetic properties, using material characterization and trapping.

Studies complex dynamical systems through theoretical, numerical, observational and experimental methods. Her astronomy research addresses planetary and satellite systems, planetesimal evolution, stars and gas in galaxies, and active galactic nuclei. Her current research narrative also identifies finite-element studies of active matter and pattern formation, granular physics relevant to rubble asteroids, low-cost robotics and quantum complexity.

Granular and active-matter dynamics
Studies granular systems relevant to rubble asteroids and uses finite-element simulations for active matter and pattern formation.

Planetary and galactic dynamics
Uses computational and theoretical methods to study planetary systems, planetesimal evolution, galaxies and orbital/spin dynamics.

Quantum complexity
Her current personal research overview identifies quantum complexity as an active direction.

Investigates and engineers genetic communication and population dynamics in microbial communities. Her lab combines systems and synthetic biology, molecular microbiology, biochemical engineering and computational modeling to understand horizontal gene transfer and build predictive tools for controlling it. Applications include antibiotic resistance, functional microbiomes in human and agricultural systems, and environmental remediation. Work on bacterial metabolism and plasmid dynamics connects genetic exchange with microbial fitness and treatment response.

Systems and synthetic biology of microbial communities
Integrates experimental and computational methods to design stable microbial systems and functional microbiomes for human, agricultural and environmental applications.

Bacterial metabolism and antibiotic response
Metabolic engineering is a stated interest; her selected research connects bacterial metabolic genes and pathways with antibiotic resistance and treatment response.

Antibiotic resistance in microbial populations
Investigates antibiotic resistance as part of controlling microbial dynamics and genetic communication.

Plasmid dynamics and horizontal gene transfer
Develops predictive principles and tools for horizontal gene transfer and genetic communication in clinical and environmental microbial systems.

Computational models of microbial dynamics
Uses mathematical modeling, bioinformatics and data-driven tools together with experiments to predict and control bacterial communities and genetic exchange.

Develops experimental methods to measure nanoscale temperature and heat transfer using luminescent materials and spectroscopy. Her group adapts super-resolution and single-particle imaging for thermal metrology and combines operando thermometry with chemical-reaction monitoring. These tools address energy transport in challenging environments, with applications in device cooling, catalysis and carbon capture.

Luminescence nanothermometry and super-resolution temperature mapping
Uses luminescent probes, spectroscopy and adapted super-resolution imaging to measure nanoscale heat transport.

Operando thermometry and reaction monitoring
Develops combined temperature and chemical-reaction measurements for catalytic and other energy-conversion environments.

Develops spectroscopic and imaging methods for biomedical diagnosis. His group uses Raman measurements to investigate bone fracture risk, elastic scattering to detect changes in individual cells, and optical methods to improve bruise detection in dark skin. The broader program applies absorption, fluorescence and scattering measurements to medical questions.

Raman spectroscopy of bone quality
Investigates noninvasive optical measurements related to fracture likelihood.

Spectroscopic biomedical diagnosis
Applies absorption, fluorescence and scattering methods to medical problems.

Single-cell elastic-scattering analysis
Studies optical signatures of subtle cellular responses to stimuli.

Optical detection of bruising in dark skin
Develops measurements to improve documentation of bruising.

Studies theoretical quantum, condensed-matter and statistical physics at small scales. His work includes weak and continuous quantum measurements, their use in quantum information processing, and methods for understanding randomness and inference in physical measurements.

Weak and continuous quantum measurement theory
Studies stochastic measurement outcomes and their relevance to quantum information.

Theoretical nanophysics and condensed matter
Investigates physical behavior as systems approach nanometer dimensions.

Statistical physics of uncertain measurements
Studies physical inference and prediction in the presence of random observations.

Studies molecular and systems mechanisms of auditory and vestibular efferent feedback, particularly cochlear outer hair cells and hearing in noise. Her research links neurotransmitter receptors with protection from acoustic overstimulation and gaze stabilization. She uses receptor cloning, biochemical and immunohistochemical analysis, confocal imaging, auditory and vestibular measurements, and viral gene transfer in animal models to investigate receptor function and potential ways to influence hearing loss.

Auditory and vestibular efferent feedback
Studies cochlear outer hair cells, hearing in noise and vestibular feedback from receptor mechanisms to systems-level behavior.

Cochlear receptor biology and gene transfer
Uses cloning, immunohistochemistry and viral-mediated expression to study nicotinic acetylcholine receptors and cochlear hair-cell function in animal models.

Auditory and vestibular physiological measurement
Uses auditory and vestibular testing, including distortion-product otoacoustic emissions, to relate efferent function to receptor expression and noise susceptibility.

Studies bacterial stress responses and engineers bacteria to produce functional materials. Her lab combines sequencing, single-molecule biophysics and biochemistry to investigate chromosome organization and protection from cellular damage. Synthetic biology and bacterial 3D printing enable patterned biofilms, living materials for plastic degradation, mineralized bacterial optics and collaborative work on microbial electron transfer for hydrogen production.

Engineered living materials and bacterial mineralization
Engineers bacteria for spatially patterned biomaterials, plastic degradation and silica-based optical structures.

Bacterial stress responses and chromosome organization
Uses sequencing, single-molecule biophysics and biochemical methods to study stress enzymes, Dps-driven chromosome reorganization and survival.

Three-dimensional printing of bacteria and biofilms
Develops hydrogel-supported bacterial printing for engineered biofilms and living materials, including collaborative microbial hydrogen-production work.

Microbial electron transfer for hydrogen production
Collaborates on engineering and printing Shewanella to improve electron transfer to quantum-dot acceptors for hydrogen generation.

Studies how computation can support collective decisions and democratic institutions. His work combines theoretical computer science, economics and AI to analyze preference aggregation, liquid and virtual democracy, and participatory budgeting, examining properties such as fairness, robustness and resistance to strategic manipulation.

Algorithmic game theory of collective decisions
Analyzes incentives, fairness and robustness in computational decision systems.

Computational social choice and democratic design
Studies preference aggregation, participatory budgeting and liquid or virtual democracy.

Designs electrocatalytic systems for energy conversion and environmental remediation by combining pulsed-laser nanomaterial synthesis with electrochemical process engineering. Her work examines catalyst interfaces, electrolyte microenvironments and water-activation mechanisms to improve reaction selectivity and energy efficiency. Applications include aqueous PFAS defluorination, selective organic electrooxidation and carbon dioxide reduction.

Electrocatalytic PFAS defluorination
Develops aqueous electrocatalytic processes targeting defluorination of PFAS contaminants.

Electrode interfaces and reactive water species
Investigates material interfaces, electrolyte microenvironments and water activation to control selectivity and energy efficiency.

Selective organic oxidation and carbon dioxide electrocatalysis
Develops selective organic electrooxidation and CO2-reduction systems through electrochemical engineering.

Pulsed-laser synthesis of nanocatalysts
Uses pulsed lasers in liquids to fabricate controlled nanomaterials for electrocatalytic systems.

Develops supramolecular assembly methods to create synthetic materials with functions inspired by living systems. His group designs adaptive capsules as protein chaperone mimics, hierarchical networks resembling extracellular matrices, and chemically controlled protein assemblies capable of responding and doing mechanical work. The program combines organic synthesis, protein expression and structural characterization of noncovalent assemblies.

Bioinspired supramolecular networks
Programs hierarchical molecular assemblies as extracellular-matrix mimics and responsive functional materials.

Adaptive supramolecular capsules for protein aggregation
Designs noncovalent capsules as synthetic chaperones to address protein misfolding and aggregation.

Controlled dissipative protein assembly
Develops chemical control of protein assembly into responsive structures, combining protein expression with structural analysis.

Develops molecules and optical tools to control and measure biomolecular interactions. His group uses molecular design and dynamic combinatorial chemistry to discover sequence-selective RNA-binding compounds and investigate protein interactions. It also develops nanostructured optical biosensors, including arrayed imaging reflectometry and photonic-crystal platforms, with multiplex detection, diagnostic sensing and integration into tissue-chip systems as applications.

Nanostructured optical biosensing
Develops arrayed imaging reflectometry and photonic-crystal sensors for quantitative biomolecular detection.

Optical sensing in microphysiological systems
The lab describes a photonic-biosensor-integrated tissue-chip project for real-time inflammatory-marker sensing.

RNA recognition and dynamic combinatorial chemistry
Uses molecular design and dynamic combinatorial chemistry to discover sequence-selective RNA-binding molecules and probes of biomolecular interactions.

Uses computational mathematics and fluid dynamics to study ocean processes across spatial scales. His research investigates mechanisms of oceanic energy transfer and develops models for stratified geophysical flows. He leads development of FlowSieve, an open-source tool for multiscale decomposition in spherical and Earth-like settings.

Multiscale ocean energy transfer
Studies multiscale oceanographic processes and mechanisms that transfer energy between scales.

FlowSieve and spherical flow decomposition
Leads development of FlowSieve for efficient multiscale decompositions on spherical/Earth-like domains.

Computational geophysical fluid dynamics
Develops and applies computational models of ocean and stratified quasi-geostrophic systems.

Develops point-of-care medical technologies for settings with limited equipment, infrastructure and specialist access. His work combines biomedical ultrasound, photogrammetry and AI to investigate diagnosis and treatment of chronic conditions, emphasizing robust, usable and affordable devices that can also inform technology in better-resourced settings.

Point-of-care biomedical ultrasound
Develops ultrasound-based diagnostic approaches for resource-constrained settings.

Photogrammetry and AI for chronic-disease assessment
Applies imaging and computational techniques to conditions including diabetic foot, cancer and Parkinson's disease.

Medical-device design for limited-resource environments
Designs technologies around affordability, robustness and reduced infrastructure needs.

Studies the noncovalent interactions that drive peptide and protein self-assembly, connecting amyloid aggregation mechanisms with functional supramolecular materials. His group investigates amyloid-beta and HIV-associated SEVI fibrils, designs peptide and small-molecule hydrogels for tissue scaffolds and other applications, and develops cyclic amphipathic peptides for oligonucleotide delivery.

Peptide and amino-acid hydrogel materials
Develops self-assembling peptides and phenylalanine derivatives as hydrogels and functional supramolecular materials.

Amyloid aggregation and peptide self-assembly
Studies physicochemical and noncovalent interactions governing amyloid-beta and SEVI peptide aggregation and fibril formation.

Cyclic peptide carriers for oligonucleotides
Develops cyclic amphipathic peptides for delivery of therapeutic oligonucleotides.

Investigates inorganic and organometallic chemistry for selective feedstock conversion and molecular separation. His group studies high-valent metal complexes, oxidation and C-H activation, and connects framework structure and dynamics to gas adsorption, diffusion and separation, including capture of fluorinated greenhouse gases.

Metal-complex chemistry for selective oxidation
Studies high-valent first-row complexes and selective C-H activation.

Dynamic porous adsorbents for gas separation
Relates framework dynamics to adsorption, diffusion and fluorinated-gas capture.

Models of metalloenzyme active sites
Investigates inorganic models connecting metal-site structure and function.

Works on high-energy and high-power laser systems, including their integration, operation and diagnostics. His documented OMEGA and OMEGA EP work is complemented by interests in adaptive optics and optical-system design, with earlier experience in semiconductor lasers and imaging or display systems.

High-power laser-system integration and diagnostics
Contributed to development and operation of OMEGA EP and laser-system science.

Adaptive optics for optical and laser systems
Lists adaptive optics alongside high-power laser and optical-system research.

Develops program-analysis and optimization methods for efficient data movement and parallel execution. His work uses mathematical and computational models of locality, including reuse distance, to guide compiler and runtime improvements, memory management and program parallelization on modern computing systems.

Compiler and runtime locality optimization
Develops automatic and guided transformations to improve locality and parallelism.

Reuse-distance analysis of memory locality
Uses formal models to characterize locality and optimize data movement through memory hierarchies.

Program parallelization and memory management
Studies analysis and optimization techniques for efficient parallel programs.

Studies computer vision and multimodal learning with a focus on understanding video. His research connects visual representations with language, audio, robotics and data science through activity recognition, video segmentation and multimodal modeling. Projects include actor-action segmentation, audio-visual generation and video storytelling; trustworthy AI is a stated research interest.

Video segmentation and activity understanding
Studies video segmentation, actor-action analysis and activity recognition.

Vision-language and audio-visual learning
Develops multimodal models for audio-visual generation, video storytelling and relationships between vision and language.

Studies multiscale mechanics of the temporomandibular joint and lower-extremity joints to understand function, injury and disease risk. Her work connects ligament and movement mechanics with clinical translation, examining how research representation and biomechanical differences affect musculoskeletal health disparities.

Temporomandibular joint and ligament biomechanics
Uses multiscale analysis to investigate jaw-joint function and dysfunction.

Lower-extremity movement and joint mechanics
Studies hip, knee and ankle biomechanics in relation to injury and disease risk.

Translation and representation in musculoskeletal research
Examines biomechanical mechanisms and research practices relevant to health disparities.

Studies peripheral vestibular function and the access of drugs to inner-ear targets involved in hearing and balance. His stated interests include inner-ear drug delivery, pharmacokinetics and pharmacological targets for auditory and vestibular dysfunction. An institutional report of his research describes auditory and vestibular recordings in mice to test whether compounds with limited central-nervous-system access can reach peripheral inner-ear targets.

Peripheral auditory and vestibular pharmacology
Studies pharmacological targets for hearing and balance and assessment of peripheral vestibular function.

Inner-ear drug access and pharmacokinetics
Official interests identify inner-ear drug delivery and pharmacokinetics; an attributed institutional report describes mouse auditory and vestibular recordings testing peripheral access of drugs with limited CNS entry.

Develops deep-learning methods for continual learning, robustness to bias and visual understanding. His work includes medical computer vision and computational pathology, language-guided scene interpretation and visual question answering, drawing on broader interests in human and machine vision.

Medical computer vision and computational pathology
Applies learning methods to biomedical images and pathology.

Continual learning and bias-robust AI
Studies learning over time and robustness to bias in artificial intelligence.

Language-guided scene understanding
Studies visual question answering and interpretation of visual scenes using language.

Object recognition, detection and segmentation
Develops vision methods spanning scene objects, tracking and active visual analysis.

Studies plasma physics for inertial-confinement fusion and astrophysical systems using high-performance computation. His stated program includes AI and machine learning alongside computational plasma methods. Selected research links particle-in-cell simulations to hot-electron generation in fusion and kinetic studies to collisionless shocks and particle acceleration.

Computational inertial-confinement fusion plasma physics
Studies laser-plasma behavior and hot-electron generation relevant to inertial-confinement fusion.

Particle-in-cell and kinetic plasma simulation
Selected research uses particle-in-cell simulations for hot-electron generation and kinetic modeling of collisionless shocks and particle acceleration.

High-performance computing for plasma astrophysics
Identifies plasma astrophysics and high-performance computing, including AI/ML, as connected research areas.

Investigates intense femtosecond laser interactions with gases, solids and plasmas. His work studies multielectron behavior in atoms and molecules under strong fields and uses laser processing to create functional material surfaces with tailored color, absorption and wetting properties.

Ultrafast strong-field atomic and molecular dynamics
Studies multielectron effects under intense femtosecond laser fields.

Femtosecond laser processing of solids
Uses laser-matter interactions to modify material surfaces.

Laser-engineered optical and wetting surfaces
Develops surfaces with altered color and hydrophilic or hydrophobic behavior.

Studies material structure and response under extreme pressure and high-energy-density conditions. Her work uses x-ray diffraction during dynamic compression, including ramp-compressed sodium and multiframe diffraction experiments. Institutional research accounts describe studies of alkali-metal electronic and ionic structure, high-strain-rate response and optical properties of extreme matter, with connections to planetary and laboratory astrophysics.

Dynamic x-ray diffraction at extreme pressure
An institutional account describes her ramp-compressed sodium experiments and contributions to multiframe x-ray diffraction.

Extreme-pressure material structure and response
Studies electronic and ionic structure of alkali metals at extreme pressure, alongside high-strain-rate material response and optical properties.

Develops statistical approaches and algorithms for language understanding and machine translation. His work includes semantic parsing and generation, with earlier contributions to pronunciation modeling, speech recognition and computational phonology.

Statistical algorithms for language understanding
Develops computational methods for interpreting and generating natural language.

Semantic parsing and structured text generation
Studies meaning representations and their connection to language generation.

Statistical machine translation
Investigates computational approaches to translating language.

Studies algorithms and mathematical structure in theoretical computer science. His research includes Markov-chain sampling and counting, graph and surface-curve problems, algorithmic game theory and applications of discrete and continuous Fourier transforms. His listed interests also connect combinatorics with learning and phylogeny.

Markov-chain sampling and counting
Studies Markov-chain sampling and counting problems in theoretical computer science.

Graph algorithms and curves on surfaces
Studies graph drawing, combinatorics and algorithmic problems on curves embedded in surfaces.

Discrete and continuous Fourier methods
Investigates applications of discrete and continuous Fourier transforms in theoretical computer science.

Algorithmic game theory
Algorithmic game theory is a stated research direction.

Develops electronic and electroactive polymers by connecting molecular structure, mechanical behavior and device performance. His research combines polymer synthesis, mechanical testing, modeling and soft-material characterization to create deformable semiconductors for flexible photovoltaics and bioelectronic sensors. He also studies organic haptics through stimulus-responsive films, contact mechanics and psychophysics, and explores nanostructured interfaces and manufacturing methods for wearable devices.

Organic haptics and tactile materials
Combines stimulus-responsive films, contact mechanics and psychophysics to investigate touch and develop haptic interfaces.

Electronic polymers and mechanical properties
Synthesizes and characterizes conducting and semiconducting polymers, linking molecular structure to deformability and electronic-device behavior under strain.

Flexible photovoltaics and thin-film interfaces
Explores stretchable solar cells, transparent electrodes and mechanically robust thin-film photovoltaics.

Wearable bioelectronic and nanostructured interfaces
Studies soft polymer interfaces and metal nanoislands on graphene for wearable sensing and cellular electrophysiology.

Develops fuel targets for inertial-confinement fusion. His research combines vapor deposition and microfluidics for polymer capsules with studies of crystal growth and cryogenic properties of deuterium-tritium fuel, including challenges of scalable target manufacture and delivery into hot reactors.

Vapor-deposited polymer capsules for fusion targets
Uses deposition methods to fabricate capsules containing fusion fuel.

Cryogenic deuterium-tritium crystal growth
Studies structure and properties of solid fusion fuel.

Microfluidic fabrication and delivery of fusion targets
Develops capsule-making methods and investigates scalable cryogenic fuel delivery.

Uses optical technology to investigate the limits of spatial and color vision and the structure and function of the living retina. His work developed adaptive optics for the eye, combining aberration correction with high-resolution retinal imaging. His research record connects optical measurements with photoreceptor mosaics, visual perception and collaborative cellular-resolution studies of retinal function and restoration.

Spatial and color vision with physiological optics
Investigates spatial/color vision and photoreceptor organization using optical methods and retinal imaging.

Adaptive-optics retinal imaging
Developed adaptive optics for ocular aberration correction and microscopic imaging of the living retina.

Cellular retinal imaging and visual function
Selected research connects cellular-resolution retinal imaging with photoreceptor organization and functional assessment of vision.

Develops ultrafast vibrational spectroscopy to track molecular structural changes during photochemical and photobiological reactions. His lab uses femtosecond stimulated Raman spectroscopy to follow charge transfer, excited-state relaxation and DNA photophysics, and develops multidimensional Raman methods to reveal vibrational coupling and energy flow through molecules.

Femtosecond stimulated Raman spectroscopy
Develops FSRS methods that resolve vibrational spectra and molecular structure during ultrafast reactions.

Excited-state structural dynamics and DNA photophysics
Measures structural dynamics during charge transfer and ultraviolet-excited DNA relaxation using time-resolved vibrational spectroscopy.

Multidimensional vibrational spectroscopy
Develops 2D-FSRS to resolve anharmonic vibrational coupling and intramolecular energy flow.

Investigates how ultrasound interacts with cells and tissues to support diagnostic imaging, engineered tissues and regenerative medicine. Her laboratory connects physical and biological mechanisms with acoustic patterning, wound-healing research and quantitative high-frequency imaging of tissue structure, mechanical properties and function.

Mechanisms of ultrasound interaction with cells and tissues
Studies molecular, cellular and physical responses relevant to ultrasound safety and therapy.

Ultrasound-enabled tissue engineering and regeneration
Develops acoustic approaches for engineered tissues, biomaterials and wound healing.

Quantitative ultrasound characterization of tissues
Develops high-frequency measurements of native and engineered tissue structure and mechanics.

Studies transport and mixing in biological and technological fluids, primarily cerebrospinal fluid and liquid metals. His work connects experiments, physical models and data analysis with brain-fluid circulation, battery-layer transport and metal processing, alongside interests in inner-ear mixing and coherent structures in reactive flows.

Transport in liquid-metal batteries and processing
Investigates how fluid motion affects liquid-metal energy storage and metal technologies.

Cerebrospinal fluid and glymphatic transport
Studies brain-fluid flow and solute movement using physical models and measurements.

Fluid mixing in the inner ear
Lists inner-ear mixing within the biophysical fluid research program.

Coherent structures and reactive mixing
Studies the fundamental organization and transport properties of mixing flows.

Designs and analyzes high-speed, low-power digital and mixed-signal integrated circuits. His research connects CMOS design and three-dimensional integration with interconnect behavior, substrate noise, clock timing and power delivery, including applications in portable processors and wireless communication electronics.

Integrated-circuit clock and power distribution
Studies synchronous timing, clock skew and power-delivery networks.

High-performance CMOS and three-dimensional circuits
Develops digital and mixed-signal IC design and analysis methods.

Interconnect and substrate-noise analysis
Investigates signal-integrity and interconnect behavior in integrated systems.

Develops quantitative models of human sensory processing from electrophysiological responses to natural speech, music and video. His work uses interpretable signal analysis to study selective attention, speech in competing sound and audiovisual integration. These methods connect computational neuroscience with noninvasive brain measurements, brain-computer interfaces and collaborative studies of sensory processing in developmental and psychiatric conditions.

Neural encoding of natural speech and sound
Models human electrophysiological responses to natural speech and music to understand sensory processing.

Attention and audiovisual speech integration
Studies selective attention in competing auditory scenes and audiovisual speech using interpretable noninvasive electrophysiological measures.

Sensory electrophysiology and brain-computer interfaces
Develops quantitative, interpretable models of neuroelectric signals, with stated interests in brain-computer interfaces and sensory disorders.

Develops optical imaging and measurement methods to investigate tumor biology in living tissue, especially breast-cancer metastasis. His work connects extracellular matrix structure, neuronal activity and stress signaling to tumor behavior, using multiphoton microscopy and second-harmonic generation to study tissue organization and prognostic optical signatures.

In-vivo multiphoton imaging of tumor biology
Develops optical methods to measure biological processes in living intact tissue.

Second-harmonic imaging of tumor extracellular matrix
Studies matrix organization and emission directionality in relation to breast-cancer progression.

Microenvironmental influences on tumor metastasis
Investigates matrix, neural activity and stress signaling as influences on metastasis.

Develops interactive AI systems that sense and interpret human behavior to support communication, education and health. His work combines machine learning, vision and behavioral modeling, including nonverbal-signal analysis and systems for social-skills and public-speaking practice.

Computational sensing of nonverbal behavior
Develops algorithms to capture subtle behavioral signals for interactive systems.

Affective interfaces for communication practice
Studies interactive technology for social skills and public speaking.

Interactive AI for health and educational access
Designs behavior-aware systems intended to improve access in healthcare and education.

Investigates structured light and nanoscale light-matter interactions, linking singular and topological optical fields with imaging, sensing and optical manipulation. Her research explores nanophotonics and metasurfaces, with applications including quantum cryptography, metrology and advanced imaging. Optical trapping, holography and biophotonics are also stated interests.

Nanophotonics and metasurfaces for structured light
Investigates nanoscale light-matter interactions and lists metasurfaces as a research interest.

Structured and singular optical fields
Studies structured light and singular/topological optics with applications to imaging, sensing, optical manipulation and quantum cryptography.

Her official department and lab entries identify research interests in cell adhesion, the mechanical and thermodynamic behavior of biological membranes, and cytoskeletal contributions to cellular mechanics. A laboratory publication listing attributes work on transient neutrophil elasticity to her. The individual faculty profile is unavailable, so a complete personal research overview and current project scope could not be established.

Cell adhesion, membrane mechanics and cytoskeletal function
Official department and lab entries identify cell adhesion, biological membrane mechanics and thermodynamics, and cytoskeletal function as her interests. These entries do not establish a particular single-cell measurement technique.

Uses synthetic inorganic chemistry to develop molecular approaches to energy storage and fuel production. Her group designs metal-oxide clusters and heterometallic catalysts to understand cooperative electron/proton transfer and small-molecule activation. Reducible metal-oxide metalloligands provide models of support effects in catalysis, while soluble polyoxovanadate complexes are investigated as multielectron electrolytes for redox-flow batteries.

Metal-oxide cluster synthesis and cooperative catalysis
Designs heterometallic catalysts and reducible metal-oxide metalloligands to study support effects and cooperative small-molecule activation.

Proton and electron transfer in polyoxovanadates
Studies coupled electron/proton transport and redox chemistry in metal-oxide clusters for substrate activation and energy conversion.

Molecular electrolytes for redox-flow batteries
Develops soluble earth-abundant polyoxovanadate cluster complexes as reversible multielectron electrolytes for flow-battery energy storage.

Develops methods to discover, integrate and acquire representative data from large heterogeneous repositories. Her work applies probabilistic and learning techniques to data management, including data-lake search and navigation, automated feature engineering and acquisition-cost optimization. She also develops scalable network-based search methods for climate data.

Data discovery and integration in heterogeneous repositories
Develops data-lake search and integration methods to find and combine datasets across large raw-data collections.

Representative data acquisition and probabilistic data management
Uses learning and probabilistic techniques for data management and optimizes costs of acquiring representative multisource datasets.

Network-based climate-data search
Develops scalable search algorithms applying network analysis to real-time climate data.

Combines microbial engineering, synthetic biology and polymer chemistry to create sustainable materials. His work uses living systems for polymer production, environmental sensing and controlled degradation, with related bioelectrochemical and bioinspired catalytic approaches to plastic upcycling and resource conversion.

Biological strategies for environmental remediation
Studies living-system approaches to sensing, degradation and sustainable material lifecycles.

Synthetic biology for polymer production and degradation
Engineers microbial processes for polymer synthesis and controlled breakdown.

Microbial metabolism-driven polymerization
Connects microbial metabolism with controlled radical polymerization.

Bioinspired catalysis and bioelectrochemistry
Studies biological strategies for chemical conversion, including DNA-directed catalyst immobilization.

Polymer chemistry and plastic upcycling
Develops routes toward circular polymer production and degradation.

Biological environmental sensing
Uses living-system approaches for environmental sensing applications.

Develops III-V semiconductor materials and optoelectronic devices, connecting molecular-beam epitaxial growth with optical and electronic properties. His work includes quantum dots, superlattices and heterostructure interfaces, studied using optical spectroscopy and material characterization. Device directions include visible and infrared lasers, infrared emitters and detectors, and semiconductor transistors.

Molecular-beam epitaxy of III-V semiconductors
Develops epitaxial growth methods and reduced-dimensional III-V structures including quantum dots, superlattices and heterostructures.

III-V optoelectronic devices and spectroscopy
Studies semiconductor optical properties and interfaces for lasers, infrared emitters/detectors and electronic devices, using Raman and photoluminescence spectroscopy.

Develops signal, image and data-analysis methods for visual computing, biomedical information and connected sensing systems. His lab studies retinal-vessel segmentation, multimodal registration, lidar/camera fusion and geospatial imagery; RNA structure prediction, flow-cytometry analytics and wearable movement measurements; and secure media, color-display design and autonomous energy-harvesting systems. These projects combine physical models, statistical learning and sensor data rather than a single generic image-integrity task.

Multimodal computer vision and retinal image analysis
Develops retinal-vessel segmentation, image registration, lidar/camera depth fusion and geospatial visual analytics.

RNA structure and flow-cytometry analytics
Uses homologous-sequence information and thermodynamic models for RNA structure estimation, and automated analysis of large flow-cytometry datasets.

Wearable movement-sensor analytics
Analyzes body-worn accelerometer data with machine learning to study progression and treatment response in movement disorders.

Media watermarking and color-imaging models
Develops robust audio watermarking and model-based color-barcode and display optimization methods.

Energy harvesting for autonomous embedded systems
Develops open-source power-harvesting designs for autonomous field-deployed systems.

Investigates matter under extreme pressure and energy density through laboratory experiments and collaborative modeling. His work connects dense planetary interiors and stellar plasmas with shock-compression measurements, material phase behavior and conditions relevant to inertial fusion, aiming to understand how matter behaves beyond ordinary chemical regimes.

Extreme-density material states and fusion conditions
Studies material behavior in high-energy-density regimes relevant to laboratory fusion.

Shock compression at planetary-interior pressures
Uses laboratory extreme-pressure experiments to investigate dense material behavior.

Laboratory microphysics of planets and stars
Investigates interior material properties, including hydrogen-helium phase behavior.

Develops statistical learning and signal-processing methods for data distributed over networks. His research combines graph signal processing, network science and decentralized optimization, with applications in dynamic network monitoring, social-data analysis and power grids. These methods address structure and inference in large connected datasets.

Graph signal processing and network analytics
Studies signals and inference on networks, including network monitoring, social data and power-grid analytics.

Decentralized statistical learning and optimization
Develops statistical learning and decentralized optimization methods for large networked datasets.

Studies complex systems using statistical physics, nonlinear dynamics, network theory and information theory. His group combines theory with data-driven analysis to investigate urban mobility and inequality, network robustness, collective decisions and adaptation, and how information supports agency and coordination across scales.

Statistical physics of complex networks
Studies robustness, evolution and interactions in infrastructure and information networks.

Urban systems and human mobility
Uses models and data to investigate city structure, mobility and socioeconomic dynamics.

Information-theoretic models of agency and adaptation
Investigates coordination, strategic behavior and emergence of meaning in complex systems.
