Models how porous structure controls deformation and membrane mechanical response.

Phase transformations in nanoscale metals
Studies structural transformations using atomistic models and related material experiments.

Multiscale simulation of metal deformation
Connects molecular dynamics, crystal plasticity and continuum descriptions of defects and interfaces.

Studies ultracold atoms and molecules through quantum optics and atomic physics. His work includes laser cooling and trapping, multicomponent Bose-Einstein condensates, light-based control of atomic motion, and experimental and theoretical investigations of atom-photon interactions and quantum measurement noise.

Optical control and cooling of atoms and molecules
Uses atom-light interactions for trapping and manipulating ultracold matter.

Quantum noise in atomic measurements
Investigates measurement fluctuations in ultracold atomic systems.

Multicomponent Bose-Einstein condensates
Studies coupled atomic species, spinor condensates and cold collisions.

Studies nanoscale light-matter interactions and uses optical methods to probe and control solid-state quantum emitters. His work connects microscopy and spectroscopy of individual nanostructures with quantum information and optical metrology. A recent institutional account also describes his group’s optical-tweezer and phonon-laser experiments, using control of mechanical motion and fluctuations for precision sensing research.

Solid-state quantum optics
Uses optics to interrogate and control artificial and naturally occurring solid-state quantum emitters.

Single-nanostructure optical microscopy and spectroscopy
Develops high-resolution microscopy and spectroscopy for electro-optic properties of individual nanostructures.

Levitated optomechanics and phonon lasers
An institutional account describes his optical-tweezer phonon-laser work and control of mechanical fluctuations for sensing.

Designs, fabricates and characterizes nanophotonic materials and devices. His work combines quantum dots and photonic-crystal structures with applications in quantum emitters and microlasers, photovoltaic conversion and optical biosensing. The lab also identifies photocatalysis and photonic biological applications as research directions, including nanowire sensors and integrated optofluidic structures described in his official appointment biography.

Quantum-dot emitters and nanophotonic lasers
Develops quantum-dot and nanostructured photonic devices, including single-photon emitters and microlasers.

Photonic nanostructures for energy and biosensing
Designs nanophotonic structures for solar cells, nanowire biosensors and optofluidic detection; the lab also studies photocatalysis.

Studies how material microstructure and processing determine properties, using microscopy and experimental design to quantify those relationships. His work extends to biological materials and mechanics, where variability motivates robust design approaches and investigation of fabrication or treatment processes.

Experimental and robust design of material processes
Uses designed experiments to investigate process performance and variability.

Variability in biomaterial mechanics
Studies biological materials and mechanical variation relevant to biomedical applications.

Microscopy of microstructure-property relationships
Quantifies material structure to connect processing with mechanical and other properties.

Develops quantum-dynamics methods to understand and control chemical reactivity. His group studies nonadiabatic electronic and nuclear motion, molecule-cavity coupling and polariton chemistry, and photoinduced proton-coupled electron transfer in solar-energy conversion, connecting electronic structure with time-dependent reaction mechanisms.

Cavity QED and polariton-mediated chemistry
Models how hybrid molecule-photon states alter chemical reaction pathways.

Quantum simulation of chemical reactivity
Develops methods connecting electronic-structure descriptions and quantum molecular dynamics.

Nonadiabatic and nuclear quantum dynamics
Studies transitions among electronic, vibrational and photonic states, including nuclear quantum effects.

Photoinduced proton-coupled electron transfer
Investigates reaction dynamics relevant to solar fuels and photocatalyst design.

Develops multiscale process-systems models that combine physical mechanisms and data to support sustainable design and operation. Her group connects molecular, particulate and process-wide behavior with product-process decisions, including powder flow and solvent-based extraction.

Sustainable process-systems decision models
Builds predictive tools for resource-efficient product and process decisions.

Powder-flow modeling
Studies particulate dynamics within multiscale process models.

Hybrid physical and data-driven process models
Combines mechanistic and learned descriptions across molecular-to-process scales.

Solvent-based extraction processes
Lists solvent extraction within the process-systems research program.

Investigates nonlinear optical, quantum optical and optomechanical phenomena in micro- and nanoscale photonic structures. His research connects the fundamental behavior of confined light and mechanical motion with nanophotonic devices for chip-scale signal processing in both classical and quantum regimes.

Chip-scale nonlinear photonic signal processing
Studies nonlinear optical phenomena in micro- and nanoscale structures for classical chip-scale photonic processing.

Quantum optical nanophotonic devices
Investigates quantum optical phenomena in micro/nanophotonic structures and their use in chip-scale quantum signal processing.

Optomechanics in micro- and nanophotonic structures
Studies coupling between optical and mechanical behavior in confined photonic structures.

Studies how sediment movement, erosion and deposition shape planetary landscapes. Her group combines theory, numerical models, field observations and physical experiments to investigate river sediment diffusion, rocky hillslope evolution and arctic-soil patterns, linking geomorphology to fluid instabilities and granular physics.

Sediment transport and landscape evolution
Studies erosion, deposition and the evolution of rivers and hillslopes.

Granular transport and pattern formation in soils
Connects arctic-soil patterns with fluid instability and granular mechanics.

Models and experiments of river and hillslope dynamics
Develops and tests landscape models using theory, fieldwork and laboratory flows.

Builds mathematical models of how populations of cortical neurons represent sensory beliefs and support decisions. His research tests probabilistic-inference and neural-sampling accounts of vision, connects neural correlations to perceptual choices, and studies binocular depth and natural-image statistics using neural and behavioral data.

Neural population coding and perceptual decisions
Relates neural variability and readout weights to behavioral choices.

Probabilistic inference models of visual perception
Tests neural-sampling accounts of how sensory data and learned expectations are combined.

Computational binocular vision and natural-image statistics
Studies how visual neurons encode depth and adapt to the structure of sensory inputs.

Studies orthopaedic tissue mechanobiology using biomaterials, multiscale mechanical models and intravital imaging. Her laboratory investigates how cells and tissues respond to loading and injury, aiming to design mechanically targeted therapies that improve healing and limit joint deterioration.

Intravital multiphoton imaging of orthopaedic tissues
Uses live-tissue imaging to investigate tissue structure and mechanobiological behavior.

Mechanically targeted therapies for joint repair
Investigates biomaterial and regenerative strategies for healing and prevention of joint deterioration.

Multiscale orthopaedic mechanotransduction
Studies mechanical responses across cells, tissues and whole-joint models.

Develops near-infrared diffuse optical methods to measure tissue function and metabolism, with an emphasis on breast-cancer detection and treatment monitoring. Her laboratory studies early optical indicators of therapy response, uses animal models to investigate metabolic mechanisms, and explores fluorescent agents that expose additional physiological information.

Near-infrared spectroscopy of tissue function
Develops diffuse optical measurements of deep-tissue functional and metabolic parameters.

Optical monitoring of breast-cancer therapy
Investigates early response indicators and metabolic mechanisms of varying treatment response.

Fluorescent agents for tissue functional measurements
Explores near-infrared agents that expose additional metabolic or functional parameters.

Develops finite-element methods for nonlinear solid and structural mechanics. His research connects computational models of developing soft and cardiac tissue with analysis of historical Roman concrete domes and vaults. Methods include large-strain hyperelastic and viscoelastic formulations, contact and fracture analysis, geometric reconstruction and adaptive meshing to study growth, deformation and structural deterioration.

Nonlinear finite-element mechanics
Develops and applies finite-element models for hyperelastic, incompressible and viscoelastic materials with large deformation.

Computational developmental biomechanics
Models soft and cardiac tissue growth, muscle contraction and developmental geometry using nonlinear FEM.

Structural mechanics of historical concrete architecture
Uses geometric reconstruction, nonlinear FEM and fracture/contact analysis to study Roman concrete domes, vaults and deterioration.

Studies thermonuclear plasma physics for magnetic and inertial confinement fusion. His documented theoretical and numerical work addresses tokamak stability and the hydrodynamic stability of imploding fuel capsules, including how ablation, density gradients and heat transport affect Rayleigh-Taylor instability and its control.

Hydrodynamic stability of inertial-fusion implosions
Analyzes capsule instability and the coupled effects of ablation, density and heat transport.

Thermonuclear plasma theory for confinement fusion
Investigates plasma behavior relevant to magnetic and inertial fusion.

Kinetic and MHD stability of tokamak plasmas
Uses analytical and numerical approaches to plasma stability.

Investigates human learning, memory and decisions using experiments and computational models. His work connects visual and multisensory perception with short-term memory and conceptual knowledge, comparing human behavior with Bayesian ideal-observer models and studying how training and limited capacity shape perception.

Computational and experimental models of perceptual memory
Studies visual learning, working memory and formation of conceptual representations.

Bayesian models of perceptual learning and decisions
Compares human behavior with ideal-observer and ideal-actor predictions.

Multisensory perception and perceptual training
Investigates learning and expertise across sensory and cognitive tasks.

Investigates nonlinear optical interactions and the optical response of materials, with applications in quantum and nonlinear imaging. His official profile describes research connections at Rochester and Ottawa; it supports optical physics, without establishing general turbulence or fluid-mechanics expertise.

Quantum and nonlinear optical imaging
Applies nonlinear optical interactions to imaging questions.

Nonlinear optical interactions in materials
Studies material optical properties and applications of nonlinear light-matter interactions.

Develops instruments and controlled fabrication methods at molecular and nanoscale dimensions. His documented work connects single-molecule mechanics and diagnostic binding measurements with surface patterning, optical manipulation, and electrospun or electrosprayed scaffolds for tissue engineering.

Electrospun and electrosprayed tissue scaffolds
Develops scaffold fabrication approaches for tissue-engineering research.

Optical micropatterning and three-dimensional polymerization
Uses spatial light modulation for optical manipulation and surface-structure formation.

Nanoscale material deposition and surface patterning
Studies controlled material placement and catalytic or biocatalytic stamping.

Single-molecule mechanics and binding measurements
Develops instruments to examine molecular forces and quantitative binding events.

Studies experimental condensed-matter and applied physics, linking superconductivity and nanoscale transport with ultrafast electronics and optoelectronics. His research includes single-photon detection and counting, optical communications, ultrafast transducers and modulators, and femtosecond electro-optic, magneto-optic and terahertz characterization of materials and devices.

Terahertz and time-resolved material characterization
Uses terahertz spectroscopy/imaging and femtosecond electro-optic and magneto-optic methods to characterize solid-state materials.

Single-photon detection and quantum communication
Studies single-photon detection and counting for optical communication and quantum applications; selected work includes superconducting detectors.

Ultrafast optoelectronic transducers and modulators
Studies ultrafast electronics and optical input/output interfacing, including transducers and modulators.

Applied superconductivity and nanoscale transport
Investigates applied/high-temperature superconductivity and quantum transport phenomena in nanoscale materials.

Studies inertial-confinement fusion and high-energy-density plasmas, with a focus on experimental diagnostics. His stated methods include x-ray, neutron and charged-particle spectroscopy and imaging, including three-dimensional diagnostics. An institutional report attributes direct-drive fusion experiments to Regan and collaborators, providing concrete context for the program.

Spectroscopic and imaging diagnostics for HED plasmas
Lists x-ray spectroscopy/imaging, neutron and charged-particle measurements and 3D diagnostic development as research interests.

Direct-drive inertial fusion experiments
An attributed institutional report describes his collaborative experimental work on direct-drive inertial confinement fusion.

Studies secure, high-performance and low-power integrated circuits. His work connects side-channel, fault-injection and covert-channel analysis with hardware countermeasures, physical unclonable functions, on-chip power conversion, clock and power distribution, and three-dimensional integration.

On-chip power conversion and distribution networks
Studies reconfigurable DC-DC converters and power or clock interconnect design.

High-performance low-power integrated circuits
Develops IC design and analysis approaches including three-dimensional integration.

Hardware attacks and countermeasures
Investigates side channels, fault injection, covert channels and physical unclonable functions.

Uses first-principles atomic modeling, data-driven analysis and graph representations to study complex solid-liquid and solid-gas interfaces. His group seeks design principles for selective thermal and electrochemical catalysts and battery chemistries, focusing on interfacial configurations, competing reactions and thermodynamic losses.

Atomic modeling of battery electrode interfaces
Studies electrode and solvent configurations, including metal-chalcogen battery systems.

Thermal and electrochemical catalyst interfaces
Investigates interfacial dynamics and design descriptors for selective conversion.

First-principles models of complex interfaces
Models solid-liquid and solid-gas atomic configurations and interactions.

Graph-based data mining for atomic design
Combines sampling, machine learning and graph representations to analyze interfacial reactions.

Uses theoretical condensed-matter physics and first-principles computation to predict structure-property relationships in quantum materials. His group studies polar metals, ferroelectrics, magnetism, superconductivity and topological phases in bulk and two-dimensional materials, superlattices and heterostructures. Collaboration with experimentalists connects calculations with observed properties; his work also includes software for elastic and mechanical-property analysis.

First-principles modeling of quantum materials
Uses density-functional theory and theoretical analysis to predict material structure-property relationships and interpret experiments.

Topological, polar and superconducting materials
Studies topological phases, polar metals, ferroelectrics, magnetism and superconductivity in bulk, 2D and heterostructured materials.

Computational elastic-property analysis
His corresponding-author software publication describes MechElastic for mechanical and elastic analysis of bulk and 2D materials.

Develops compilers and performance models for programs running on heterogeneous CPU/GPU systems. His research focuses on optimizing irregular and graph algorithms on GPUs, connecting computer architecture, programming-language implementation and empirical performance analysis.

Optimizing compilers for irregular GPU algorithms
Develops compiler transformations and programming-language implementations to improve irregular and graph-program performance.

Performance models for heterogeneous CPU/GPU systems
Studies accelerator-based systems and models graph-algorithm performance on GPUs.

Develops ultrasound imaging methods that use tissue motion and mechanical response to reveal contrast absent from conventional images. His work combines ultrasound-tissue interaction, echo statistics, signal processing and motion tracking for elasticity imaging, including acoustic radiation force and shear-wave approaches. He also investigates magnetically induced motion imaging of implanted brachytherapy seeds and methods that could guide therapeutic delivery.

Ultrasound elastography and acoustic radiation force
Develops ARFI, spatially modulated ultrasound radiation force and single-tracking-location shear-wave methods to image tissue mechanical response.

Ultrasound motion tracking and echo analysis
Studies echo statistics and signal processing to measure physiological or induced tissue motion and enhance imaging contrast.

Ultrasonic localization of brachytherapy seeds
Investigates magnetically induced vibration and ultrasound tracking to improve localization of implanted seeds.

Combines experimental quantum-materials research with nanoscale electronic-device engineering. His program develops spintronic structures to generate, detect and manipulate spin currents, synthesizes complex-oxide thin films and investigates two-dimensional electronic systems for controllable topological devices. The aim is to connect emergent material properties with electronics beyond conventional scaling.

Quantum-material electronic devices
Connects quantum materials with nanoscale device engineering and functional complex-oxide thin films.

Spin-current generation and manipulation
Studies spintronic devices for nanoscale spin-current generation, detection and control.

Two-dimensional topological electronic systems
Investigates 2D electronic systems for controllable topological devices.

Investigates how the structure, biomechanics and optics of the eye determine retinal image quality and visual perception. Her lab develops adaptive-optics visual simulators, multiphoton microscopy, quantitative optical coherence tomography and dynamic imaging to measure ocular geometry, collagen organization and aberrations. Imaging, psychophysics and modeling support studies of corneal disease, lens aging and myopia, and the design and selection of optical corrections and intraocular lenses.

Ocular aberrations and biomechanical imaging
Measures ocular structure, aberrations and corneal/scleral biomechanics using optical imaging and quantitative OCT.

Ophthalmic lens design and visual function
Combines imaging, modeling and psychophysics to study corneal disease, lens aging, myopia and customized intraocular-lens selection.

Adaptive-optics visual simulation
Develops polychromatic adaptive-optics systems and visual simulators to test vision under controlled optical conditions.

Develops first-principles and radiation-hydrodynamic models of matter under extreme pressure, density and laser fields. His research connects equations of state, transport, opacity and stopping power with inertial-fusion implosion design, and develops quantum simulation methods for ultrafast atomic, molecular and plasma dynamics.

Theory of strong-field and attosecond dynamics
Studies ultrafast ionization and radiation in laser interactions with atoms, molecules, solids and plasmas.

Radiation-hydrodynamic modeling of fusion implosions
Uses first-principles material properties to analyze target instability and thermonuclear burn.

First-principles properties of dense matter
Computes equations of state, transport, opacity and stopping power using quantum molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo methods.

Quantum-dynamics and numerical-method development
Develops time-dependent density-functional, finite-element and hydrodynamic-grid methods.

Develops room-temperature single-photon sources for quantum communication using quantum nanophotonics, liquid crystals and single-emitter microscopy. Her work combines confocal fluorescence and atomic-force microscopy, nanoplasmonics and nanofabrication to control photon polarization and propagation in photonic structures. Earlier work addressed nonlinear liquid-crystal optics and high-power laser beam shaping. She also develops quantum and nano-optics teaching experiments and studies the history of optics.

Quantum and nano-optics teaching experiments
Created and teaches laboratory courses in quantum optics, quantum information and nano-optics.

Single-photon sources and liquid-crystal nanophotonics
Develops room-temperature single-emitter photon sources, using microscopy and nanofabrication to study polarization and propagation in liquid-crystal photonic structures.

Nonlinear liquid-crystal optics and laser beam shaping
Her documented earlier research includes nonlinear refraction, optical power limiting, cholesteric lasers and high-power beam-profile control.

Studies optical polarization and metrology, including stress-engineered optical elements, nanostructures and polarization in single-molecule microscopy. His research and technical leadership also address polarization monitoring, testing and packaging of photonic integrated circuits, connecting optical-field control to imaging and manufactured photonic systems.

Freeform optical metrology
Lists freeform optical measurement within the optical-engineering research program.

Photonic-circuit polarization, testing and packaging
Works on polarization monitoring and assembly-related evaluation of integrated photonic devices.

Stress-engineered polarization optics and microscopy
Studies structured optical fields and their use in single-molecule imaging.

Develops optical methods for photodynamic treatment of infections and tumors, combining light-transport measurements with patient-specific treatment planning. His laboratory also develops diffuse spectroscopy analysis and calibration, and automated medical-image segmentation for abscess treatment and studies of neonatal lung development.

Photodynamic therapy of infection and tumors
Studies light and drug dosing, delivery and treatment planning for antimicrobial and oncological applications.

Diffuse spectroscopy for tissue optical properties
Models reflectance and fluorescence to estimate tissue properties and photosensitizer concentration.

Medical-image segmentation for treatment and lung research
Develops automated CT segmentation of abscesses and neonatal airways.

Studies synthesis and optical properties of semiconductor nanocrystals and carbon nanotubes, linking composition, size and structure to behavior. His group investigates colloidal synthesis mechanisms, single-particle spectroscopy, nanocrystal photocatalysis and solar fuels, and coupling nanocrystals to optical cavities for polariton chemistry.

Nanocrystal-cavity coupling and polariton photophysics
Studies hybrid light-matter states and their possible use in controlling reactions.

Synthesis and characterization of colloidal semiconductors
Investigates precursor chemistry and nanoscale structure-property relationships.

Single-particle optical and electrostatic characterization
Uses optical spectroscopy and force microscopy to study nanotubes and doped nanoparticles.

Nanocrystal photocatalysis and solar-fuel chemistry
Collaboratively studies light-driven hydrogen generation and carbon-carbon bond formation.

Uses computational physics and fluid-mechanical analysis to investigate plasma behavior and hydrodynamic instability. His attributed work includes nonlinear Rayleigh-Taylor evolution, electron heat transport in laser-produced plasmas and design studies for direct-drive inertial-fusion implosions.

Hydrodynamic instability in inertial-fusion design
Investigates instability and target-design questions for direct-drive fusion.

Computational plasma and fluid dynamics
Uses computational physics and differential-equation methods for plasma and flow problems.

Electron thermal transport in laser-produced plasmas
His attributed research examines electric-field effects on plasma heat transport.

Studies thermonuclear plasmas and inertial-confinement fusion, using statistical and machine-learning methods to connect simulations with experimental observations. His documented work examines discrepancies between predicted and measured implosions to test physical hypotheses and improve experimental design under limited-data conditions.

Machine-learning reconciliation of fusion simulations and data
Analyzes prediction-experiment gaps to improve models and test physical hypotheses.

Statistical analysis and design of inertial-fusion implosions
Uses empirical and theoretical information to guide fusion experiments.

Thermonuclear plasma and high-energy-density physics
Lists thermonuclear plasma and inertial-confinement fusion among his scientific interests.

Connects finite-element structural analysis with optical-system performance and design. His documented work includes optimization of precision optical structures, thermomechanical effects and integrated optomechanical analysis, including segmented or adaptive optics.

Finite-element optomechanical analysis
Translates mechanical deformation predictions into optical design and performance analysis.

Optimization of precision optical structures
Uses nonlinear programming and optical performance criteria in structural design.

Thermomechanical analysis of optical systems
His attributed work addresses structural and thermal effects on optics.

Studies ultrafast nonlinear optics and biomedical applications of light. His recent documented work includes laser-written refractive changes in ophthalmic materials and multispectral birefringence imaging for surgical nerve visualization and microplastic detection, alongside a longer background in telecommunications and optics education.

Ultrafast nonlinear optical methods
Develops ultrafast optics with biomedical and vision-related applications.

Laser-induced refractive correction in ophthalmic materials
Studies customized refractive-index changes in hydrogels and other biocompatible optical materials.

Femtosecond modification of optical materials
Uses laser writing and micromachining for vision-related material modification.

Multispectral birefringence imaging
Investigates nerve visualization and detection of microplastics in environmental samples.

Develops nanoscale catalysts and energy-storage devices by connecting material structure and interfaces with reaction mechanisms and durability. His group uses spatially resolved scanning transmission electron microscopy and spectroscopy to investigate electronic and structural dynamics, then applies those insights to catalytic materials for energy, water and environmental problems. Machine learning for materials science is also a stated interest.

Energy-storage materials and devices
Develops battery devices and investigates material interfaces and dynamics relevant to energy conversion and storage.

Nanoscale heterogeneous catalyst mechanisms
Develops durable catalysts and studies structural/electronic origins of catalytic behavior.

Spatially resolved electron microscopy and spectroscopy
Uses STEM and spectroscopy to study interfacial properties and electronic/structural dynamics of catalytic materials.

Studies how mechanical loading is converted into biochemical signals in joint cells and how this mechanotransduction influences tissue maintenance, degeneration and regeneration. His research focuses on mechanically activated ion channels, including Piezo channels, in articular chondrocytes and other musculoskeletal cells. His experimental background connects single-protein force measurements with single-cell biophysics, with osteoarthritis mechanisms and potential interventions as a central application.

Mechanically activated ion channels in joint cells
Investigates Piezo and other mechanically activated channels linking joint loading to cell signaling in physiological and pathological conditions.

Chondrocyte and cartilage mechanobiology
Studies mechanotransduction in articular chondrocytes, ligament cells, synoviocytes and chondrogenic stem cells to understand joint maintenance and degeneration.

Single-molecule force and cell biophysics
His documented experimental background combines force measurements on single proteins with single-cell studies of mechanical responses.

Investigates experimental and theoretical nonlinear optics, including ultrafast pulsed lasers and coherent interactions between light and sound. His group applies these methods to deep-tissue imaging, RF photonics, networking and quantum information. It also explores optical computing platforms for low-power information processing and optical control of acoustic waves.

Light-sound interactions for RF photonics
Studies photon-phonon interactions with applications to RF photonics and quantum information.

Ultrafast nonlinear optics and pulsed lasers
Investigates ultrafast nonlinear optics and pulsed laser systems for applications including deep brain imaging.

Coherent photon-phonon and acoustic-wave control
Studies coherent light-sound interactions and optical methods for controlling acoustic waves.

Optical computing platforms
Explores optical platforms for low-power information processing.

Studies high-intensity short-pulse laser-matter interactions and experimental diagnostics for inertial-confinement fusion and high-energy-density physics. An official research account describes his experiments on suprathermal electron generation and transport in fusion plasmas, including fast-ignition and shock-ignition work.

High-energy-density plasma diagnostics
Identifies diagnostic development for HED physics as a research direction.

Short-pulse laser-plasma interaction and electron transport
Studies high-intensity short-pulse interactions; an institutional account attributes experiments on suprathermal electron generation and transport in fast/shock ignition.

Develops polymer thin films, coatings and interfaces for electrochemical energy storage and other material applications. His group uses solution and vacuum synthesis, especially initiated chemical vapor deposition, to control composition, conformality and thickness. Battery research focuses on protective electrode interfaces, lithium-metal reversibility and solid-state electrolytes; selected work also addresses porous separators and optical polymer coatings.

Initiated chemical vapor deposition of polymer films
Uses solution and vacuum deposition, especially iCVD, for composition-controlled conformal polymer films and in situ thickness control.

Lithium-metal battery protective interfaces
Develops thin electrode coatings to suppress parasitic reactions and improve lithium-metal reversibility, safety and energy density.

Polymer electrolytes and battery separators
Studies polymer electrolyte films, solid-state battery materials and porous separators; selected work documents their electrochemical and mechanical behavior.

Optical polymer thin-film coatings
Selected research develops high-index, antireflection and permeation-barrier polymer coatings for optical applications.

Develops methods to generate and detect free-space terahertz radiation using ultrafast optics. His research examines THz-wave interactions with matter and applications of terahertz beams, connecting nonlinear optics, laser physics and optical measurement.

Terahertz-wave interaction with matter
Studies interaction of THz radiation with matter and applications of free-space terahertz beams.

Ultrafast terahertz generation and detection
Uses ultrafast optics to generate and detect free-space THz radiation.

Studies computer architecture and security to build systems that are both efficient and resistant to attack. Her work investigates CPU and GPU side channels, memory exploitation, machine-learning security and GPU architectures, connecting low-level hardware behavior with software security boundaries.

GPU architecture and security
Studies GPU systems, including return-oriented programming and side-channel vulnerabilities.

Memory exploitation and microarchitectural side channels
Investigates security weaknesses arising from memory and processor behavior.

Hardware-software security boundaries
Studies architectural mechanisms relevant to secure computing systems.

Machine-learning system security
Lists security of machine learning among her architecture and cybersecurity research topics.

Combines molecular dynamics, quantum chemistry and machine learning to design materials for carbon management. Her laboratory studies polymer membranes for CO2 separation, solvents for CO2 capture and transport, and catalysts for converting CO2 into other chemicals, linking molecular calculations to material design.

Computational design of CO2-separation membranes
Uses molecular calculations and learning methods to design gas-separating polymer materials.

Molecular simulation of polymers and solutions
Uses molecular dynamics to generate data connecting molecular structure and material behavior.

Quantum-chemical modeling of solvation and reactions
Calculates solvated molecular processes to inform material and catalyst design.

Machine learning for molecular material design
Combines simulation-derived data and AI for sustainability applications.

Computational CO2 conversion and solvent design
Designs catalysts for CO2 conversion and solvents for its capture and transfer.

Co-designs computer systems and architecture with sensing and human perception. His work connects hardware and software for visual computing with imaging, rendering and display, extended reality, embodied AI and autonomous agents. Earlier work emphasized efficient mobile systems and web technologies; his current program centers on how computers sense the physical world and present information to people.

Sensing and visual-computing systems co-design
Co-designs computer systems with physical sensing, imaging and visual-computing workloads.

Extended-reality computing systems
Studies computing systems for XR that integrate sensing with information presented for human perception.

Perception-aware computer architecture
Connects computer architecture and software design with human perceptual systems and quality of experience.

Studies human-computer interaction in mixed reality by modeling and supporting user behavior and perception. His research combines computational sensing of behavioral patterns with new input techniques, adaptive interfaces and embodied virtual interactions. Work explores how virtual and physical context can shape communication, body ownership and interaction in augmented and virtual environments.

Computational modeling of mixed-reality user behavior
Captures behavioral and perceptual patterns with computational methods to understand and enhance mixed-reality interaction.

Embodied input and adaptive interfaces
Develops input techniques and adaptive interfaces, including embodied interactions and links between physical and virtual context.

Mixed-reality perception and behavioral interaction
Studies perception and behavior in VR/AR, including relationships between user movement and virtual representation.

Investigates surface and materials science for hydrogen-isotope containment and separation in fusion fuel systems. His experimental research develops thin-film materials, interfaces and instrumentation, including 2D materials and atomic-layer-deposited oxides, nitrides and nanolaminates. He works with theory and computation to understand material interactions; earlier research addressed graphene synthesis and thin-film electronic materials.

Atomic layer deposition and ultrathin material interfaces
Develops ALD oxides, nitrides and nanolaminates and studies 2D materials for interface-controlled material behavior.

Hydrogen-isotope material interactions
Studies material interactions relevant to hydrogen-isotope containment and separation.

Experimental instrumentation for fusion fuel materials
Develops materials-synthesis and characterization instrumentation for fusion-fuel material studies.

Designs analog VLSI and mixed-signal circuits for sensing and imaging. His work includes sigma-delta analog-to-digital converters, low-power sensor interfaces, pixel-level conversion in digital image sensors and focal-plane compression, with attention to noise, distortion and computational efficiency.

Low-noise sigma-delta conversion and sensor interfaces
Develops converter and interface architectures addressing offset, noise and distortion.

Pixel-level conversion and compression in image sensors
Designs integrated imaging architectures and focal-plane processing methods.

Creates embodied and intelligent interfaces to support learning, communication and wellbeing for people with varied abilities and backgrounds. Her human-computer interaction research combines augmented reality, tangible interfaces, conversational agents, collaborative learning and assistive technology, including machine-learning approaches to human interaction.

Machine learning for human-computer interaction
Uses learning methods to investigate human interaction and collaborative learning behavior.

Embodied conversational agents for learning
Develops interactive agents to support communication and technology-enhanced learning.

Augmented reality and tangible learning interfaces
Creates embodied interfaces for learning and communication across differing user needs.

Assistive and collaborative interaction design
Studies interfaces supporting people with diverse abilities in shared learning activities.

Develops computer-audition methods that interpret music, speech and environmental sound. His work combines signal processing and machine learning for transcription, source separation, speech enhancement, sound retrieval and audiovisual performance analysis, including interactive systems for human-computer music making.

Music transcription and audiovisual performance analysis
Studies audio-score alignment, transcription and multimodal analysis of musical performance.

Speech and sound analysis with machine learning
Develops methods for source separation, speech enhancement and emotion analysis.

Audio retrieval and music recommendation
Investigates sound search, query-by-example and music annotation or recommendation.

Human-computer collaborative music making
Develops interactive music systems informed by computer audition.

Studies transport phenomena and computational fluid dynamics, including nanoparticle-coated microtubes for capturing cells in flowing blood. His work also includes computational approaches to transport equations and teaching materials that explain fluid-mechanics principles, connecting chemical-engineering fundamentals with biomedical transport applications.

Transport phenomena and computational fluid dynamics
Studies fluid and transport behavior using chemical-engineering and computational methods.

Cell capture in flowing microtubes
Investigates nanoparticle coatings that enhance capture of cells from flow.

Fluid-mechanics educational visualization
Develops curricular video materials explaining fundamental flow principles.

Her official profile identifies research interests in shape-memory polymers, polymer composites and biomaterials, including degradation, controlled drug delivery and structure-property relationships. She directs chemical engineering teaching laboratories and teaches process analysis, laboratory practice and senior design. The profile does not provide a substantive research overview explaining current projects or methods.

Shape-memory polymers and polymer structure-property interests
The official individual profile states interests in shape-memory polymers, composites, biomaterials, degradation and structure-property relationships; it does not describe a current experimental program.

Controlled drug delivery interest
Controlled drug delivery is an explicitly stated official research interest; the page supplies no specific platform, method or current project.

Chemical engineering laboratory instruction
Directs teaching laboratories and teaches chemical engineering laboratory practice, process analysis and senior design.

science.description: The U.S. Army Research Office (ARO) in partnership with NSA’s Laboratory for Physical Science (LPS) is soliciting Incubator, Collaboration, and Fellowship research proposals for participation in the LPS Qubit Collaboratory (LQC). The mission of the LQC can be captured in three broad goals: 1) pursue disruptive fundamental research and enabling technologies with a focus on qubit development for quantum computing and other applications (such as sensing); 2) grow deep, collaborative partnerships to tackle the most difficult and relevant long-term problems in quantum information science and technology; and 3) build a quantum workforce of tomorrow through research experiences in government at LPS and at LQC partners. The LQC will offer a mechanism for collaborative research between LPS and academia, industry, FFRDCs, and Government Laboratories to advance foundational and transformative research on challenging problems that have hindered progress in quantum information processing and associated technologies. The goal of this BAA is to seek proposals that bring together expertise from the public and private sectors and their respective research infrastructures to advance solutions that may be best approached as a collaborative team. A Collaboratory is “a center without walls, in which the nation’s researchers can perform their research without regard to physical location, interacting with colleagues, accessing instrumentation, sharing data and computational resources, [and] accessing information in digital libraries. This BAA introduces LQC Research Thrusts (A.1.1) which are the technical areas of interest—which will be updated periodically—where partners of the LQC will pursue joint research with LPS through Incubator (A.1.2) and Collaboration (A.1.3) collaborative agreements. The LQC BAA also fulfills the Government’s overarching interest--through the proposed research and on-site research experiences--in creating and training a workforce in quantum science and technology, generating pathways of solutions that feed technology development, establishing partnerships, and creating transition opportunities. In further support of training through research, Section A.1.4 calls for Quantum Computing Research (QuaCR) Graduate and Postdoctoral Fellowships for US citizens working in areas of interest. Substantial progress on solving the most difficult and long-term Quantum Information Science & Technology (QIST) research problems that unleash further rapid progress in the field will constitute LQC success. Examples of such research problems include (but are not limited to): limits of performance due to device design, material selection, and/or control, the exploration of alternative qubit physics (e.g., different approaches to qubit encoding or types of gates) and lowering of barriers to such approaches, advances in materials that improve qubit gate fidelity, reducing the overhead of classical components in quantum information technology and optimizing classical performance, and the exploration of applications of quantum technologies to new domains. Three categories of proposals are sought for this BAA:1. Incubator opportunities seek partnership proposals from single investigators and small research groups, including teaching colleges, who may have unique skillsets to contribute toward the pursuit of the research thrusts presented in A.1.1. Incubator proposals may also be the development of concepts into a detailed technical research approach to advance solution of problems of high interest to quantum information science research. Incubator proposals would avail themselves of the collaboration opportunities with LPS research staff and infrastructure made available at the Laboratory for Physical Sciences (LPS) to lay the groundwork for concepts that may be suitable for a Collaboratory proposal or responses to other DoD quantum information science research opportunities.2. Collaboratory proposals seek research proposals that bring together a strong significant collaboration--researchers from academia, industry, FFRDCs, and/or Government Laboratories--to pursue long-term projects focused on fundamental problems of interest to qubit development and/or associated science and technology. These collaborative groups will propose to work together in a focused manner for a period of time expected to be one to three years in order to demonstrate a proof-of-concept experiment and/or theory exploration to determine the feasibility of their creative idea.3. QuaCR Research Fellowship proposals seek to support talented U.S. citizen graduate students and postdoctoral researchers in the field of quantum information processing (primary interest) and quantum sensing (secondary interest). Applicants with a background from either within or outside QIS are encouraged. The proposed research areas are described in this BAA and must enhance active Quantum Information Science research efforts being supported by the Army Research Office and/or LPS. Research fellows are encouraged to complete an LPS Internship during their graduate career or visit during their postdoctoral fellowship. Funding Opportunity Title: LPS Qubit Collaboratory Special Research Topics Announcement: W911NF21S0009-SPECIALNOTICE-1The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM), Army Research Laboratory (ARL)-Army Research Office (ARO) is looking for proposed research and development solutions under the Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) W911NF21S0009-2 for Basic and Applied Scientific Research in Quantum Computing. The title for this Special Notice is “LPS Qubit Collaboratory Special Topics.” Upon receipt, compliant proposals will be reviewed through a technical and programmatic process in accordance with the evaluation criteria referenced in the W911NF21S0009-2 LQC BAA to determine which proposal may be awarded Grant, Cooperative Agreement, or Procurement Contract under this topic.

science.description: The purpose of this combined Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 35 and Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) under 2 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 200.204 (henceforth referred to as “BAA”) is to solicit research proposals for submission to the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Army Research Laboratory (ARL) for funding consideration. Prior to this announcement, ARL announced two separate BAAs to support the mission: 1) W911NF-17-S-0002 titled “Army Research Laboratory Army Research Office Broad Agency Announcement for Fundamental Research”; and 2) W911NF-17-S-0003 titled “Army Research Laboratory Broad Agency Announcement for Basic and Applied Scientific Research”. This announcement succeeds BAA W911NF-17-S-0002 and BAA W911NF-17-S-0003 combining the opportunities into a single announcement. ARL’s mission as the Army’s foundational research laboratory is to Operationalize Science to ensure overmatch in any future conflict. ARL’s foundational research mission spans basic research (budget activity 6.1) and applied research (budget activity 6.2) as defined by 32 CFR 22.105 but may include advanced technology development (budget activity 6.3) and advanced component development and prototypes (budget activity 6.4) when opportunities arise to directly or indirectly help achieve ARL’s mission. ARL partners across the national security enterprise to deliver fundamentally advantageous change that is rooted in the creation and exploitation of scientific knowledge. This publication constitutes a BAA for awards as contemplated in FAR 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 as well as a merit-based, competitive procedure in accordance with the Department of Defense Grant and Agreement Regulations (DoDGARS) at 32 CFR 22.315(a) and the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment Other Transaction Guide version 2.0 dated July 2023. This BAA document, and the online list of research topics found on the ARL BAA topics website at https://www.arl.devcom.army.mil/opportunities/arl-baa/, sets forth ARL’s research topics of interest for whitepapers and proposals. This BAA is issued under FAR 6.102(d)(2), which provides for the competitive selection of basic and applied research proposals, and 10 U.S.C. 4001, 10 U.S.C. 4021, and 10 U.S.C. 4022, which provide the authorities for issuing awards under this announcement for basic and applied research. The definitions of basic and applied research may be found at 32 CFR 22.105. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA and selected for award are considered to be the result of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provision of Public Law 98-369, “The Competition in Contracting Act of 1984” and subsequent amendments.
